definition: Hemispheric lateralization is the tendency for the two cerebral hemispheres to contribute differently to mental functions. In the memory literature summarized here, it refers to the view that the left temporal lobe is more involved in verbal memory and the right temporal lobe is more involved in nonverbal memory, although this pattern has been refined and questioned over time.
